'''''Anthyllis vulneraria''''',<ref>[https://plants.usda.gov/java/profile?symbol=ANVU ''Anthyllis vulneraria''] at [https://plants.usda.gov/ USDA PLANTS Database]</ref> the '''common kidneyvetch''', '''kidney vetch'''<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |access-date=2014-10-17 }}</ref> or '''woundwort'''<ref name = GRIN>{{GRIN}}</ref> is a [[medicinal plant]]<ref>[http://www.pfaf.org/database/plants.php?Anthyllis+vulneraria ''Anthyllis vulneraria''] at [[Plants For A Future]]</ref> native to Europe, northern Africa, and Western Asia.<ref name = powo/> The specific epithet ''vulneraria'' means 'wound healer'.<ref>Wolfgang Hensel, ''350 Plantes médicinales'' (french edition: Delachaux et Niestlé SA, Paris, 2008, {{ISBN|978-2-603-01531-5}}; German edition 2007 Franckh-Kosmos Verlags-GmbH & Co, Stuttgart, Wolfgang Hensel, Welche Heilpflanze ist das?)</ref>

==Description==
''Anthyllis vulneraria'' reaches {{convert|5|-|40|cm}} in height. The stem is simple or more often branched. The leaves are imparipinnate, glabrous or with scattered hairs on the upper face and silky hairs on the underside. The flower heads are spherical in shape and {{convert|10|-|20|mm}} long. The petals are yellow in most sub-species, but red in ''A. vulneraria'' var. ''coccinea''. Flowering takes place between June and September. The fruit is a legume. The fruits ripening takes place from July to October.

Kidney vetch is the [[Larval food plants of Lepidoptera|food plant]] of the [[small blue|small blue butterfly]] [[larva]]e and the [[leaf miner]], ''[[Aproaerema anthyllidella]]''.<ref>{{cite web|last=Kimber|first=Ian|title=843 ''Aproaerema anthyllidella''|url=https://ukmoths.org.uk/show.php?bf=843|publisher=UKMoths|access-date=15 April 2014}}</ref>

==Distribution and habitat==
This plant is sporadic throughout Europe, from [[Iceland]] to the [[Mediterranean]], in Asia Minor up to [[Iran]], in North Africa and in [[Ethiopia]]. It is naturalized in North America. It prefers dry grasslands and rocky environments with [[calcareous]] soil, up to {{cvt|3000|m|ft|abbr=on}} in elevation.
